title: Koszul Hom complexes compare with derived sections on a principal-open cover
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], choose $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$, put $U=D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_r)$, and let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules representing $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Write $M^\bullet=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\bullet)$. For each $e\ge1$, let $K^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ be the cochain Koszul complex and set $I^i(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)=K^{i-1}(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ for $i\le0$ and $0$ for $i>0$, with the negative Koszul differential. Then the canonical map of total complexes $\varinjlim_e\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e),M^\bullet)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\bullet)$ obtained by the Koszul-to-alternating-Cech comparison is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: By the affine module/sheaf identification, write $M^\bullet=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F^\bullet)$. For each $e$, the shifted Koszul complex $I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ is bounded and finite free. The transition $I^\bullet(f_1^{e+1},\ldots,f_r^{e+1})\to I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ multiplies the basis vector indexed by a subset $J$ by $\prod_{j\in J}f_j$; precomposition gives the filtered system of Hom complexes. The Koszul-to-alternating-Cech map sends a cochain to the corresponding localized cochains, and this multiplication makes these maps commute with the transition maps and with the Koszul and Cech differentials. By [lem-sc-affine-koszul-hom-alternating-cech], the induced map from $\varinjlim_e\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e),M^\bullet)$ to the alternating Cech total complex with $p$-th row $\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}M^\bullet_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{i=1}^rD(f_i)$. It is a finite open covering, and $D(f_{i_0})\cap\cdots\cap D(f_{i_p})=D(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p})$ is affine, isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}})$ (Stacks Tag 01HS). The restriction $\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$ is a complex of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules, with no boundedness assumption. Hence [lem-sc-qcoh-complex-alternating-cech-derived-sections] applies to $U$, $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$: the canonical map $\operatorname{Tot}(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^\bullet|_U))\to R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$, hence in $D(A)$ via $A\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, functorially in $\mathcal F^\bullet$.

proof.text: For each $i_0<\cdots<i_p$, since $\mathcal F^q\cong\widetilde{M^q}$ on the affine scheme $X$ (Stacks Tag 01IA), the sections over $D(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p})$ are $\Gamma(D(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}),\widetilde{M^q})=M^q_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$ (Stacks Tag 01HV). Restriction from a larger principal intersection is the canonical localization map, so these identifications commute term by term with every Cech face map and with the differentials of $M^\bullet$, hence identify $\operatorname{Tot}(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^\bullet|_U))$ with the module total complex of step 1. Composing the quasi-isomorphism of step 1 with the isomorphism of step 2 gives the canonical map of the item, which is therefore a quasi-isomorphism (an isomorphism in $D(A)$). With the empty-cover convention, $r=0$ gives the zero alternating Cech complex and the corresponding colimit is zero; if $\mathcal F^\bullet=0$, both complexes are zero.
